supporting_clues: Separate keratotic scale from pearly/translucent or rolled-border cues.

opposing_clues: Absence of clear pearly/rolled-border or translucency weakens BCC confidence.

guidance.label: ACK / SEK
supporting_clues: Explicitly contrast stuck-on/waxy/verrucous clues against flatter actinic roughness.
State whether the lesion reads as sharply demarcated keratotic plaque versus more actinic field-type change.
opposing_clues: Scale alone is not enough to favor ACK when waxy or stuck-on cues dominate.
Seborrheic-looking keratin does not exclude ACK if actinic roughness and malignant-risk context remain active.
required_missing_evidence: Missing closer surface texture and border-demarcation detail.
Missing confirmation of waxy/stuck-on appearance versus flatter actinic roughness.
watch_outs: Do not use keratin or scale as a shortcut to either ACK or SEK.
Do not hide uncertainty when stuck-on/waxy morphology is not clearly seen.

Patient's medical history helps in understanding the context and potential progression of the lesion.
impact_on_differential: Surface and border inspection details help in differentiating between benign and malignant lesions, which is critical for narrowing down the differential.
Dermoscopy can reveal specific patterns that are characteristic of certain types of skin cancers, aiding in the differential diagnosis.
Patient's medical history provides important context, such as whether the lesion is new or has changed over time, which can influence the differential diagnosis.
